response.sql: WITH state_totals AS (SELECT c.State AS State, SUM(i.Total) AS state_total, COUNT(*) AS invoice_count FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId WHERE i.InvoiceDate > '2010-06-22 00:00:00' AND i.InvoiceDate < '2012-06-26 00:00:00' GROUP BY c.State) SELECT SUM(state_total) AS total_of_state_totals, AVG(invoice_count) AS avg_invoices_per_state FROM state_totals;

assumptions.assumption: Grouping by c.State puts all customers with a NULL State into one group, as SQL GROUP BY does.
The average is taken over state groups (including the NULL-state group), not over customers or invoices.
State values are used as stored; empty strings or differently cased or padded spellings of the same state are treated as separate groups.
InvoiceDate is stored in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' text form, so the text comparison matches the requested date-ordering.
